account: Just before 4 a.m. on 8 November 2023, a passenger on a Metro bus in Hollywood reported an armed man aboard. The bus was at Melrose and Western avenues. The driver pulled over and evacuated the other passengers. Officers got no response from the man, and a two-hour standoff followed (Los Angeles Times via Police1, 9 November 2023). The quarterly report of the Los Angeles Police Department (LAPD) says that patrol officers tried to talk with the man for about 75 minutes. They then declared an armed barricade and called the special weapons and tactics (SWAT) team. The LAPD sent in its Boston Dynamics Spot quadruped. The report states that a drone observed the sleeping man and the suspected gun before the quadruped entered. It adds that SWAT chose the quadruped because a tracked robot could not have climbed the bus steps. The report states that the quadruped climbed the bus steps and formed a barrier between the man and the suspected firearm. It does not describe the robot removing the weapon. The man woke, left the bus and was taken into custody about 6:40 a.m. The weapon was a BB gun (Police1). Police1 attributes the initial observation to the quadruped’s camera. International Business Times' October 2024 account says that the robot removed the gun. Deputy Chief David Kowalski approves each use. The robot cost nearly $300,000 (NBC). By 1 January 2025 SWAT had deployed the robot at least seven times, Spectrum News reported.

Officers then deployed the quadruped to climb the bus steps and form a barrier between him and the weapon, later identified as a BB gun. The original LAPD report does not describe an autonomous tactical decision or the robot removing the gun.

fields.account: Just before 4 a.m. on 8 November 2023, a passenger on a Metro bus in Hollywood reported an armed man aboard. The bus was at Melrose and Western avenues. The driver pulled over and evacuated the other passengers. Officers got no response from the man, and a two-hour standoff followed (Los Angeles Times via Police1, 9 November 2023). The quarterly report of the Los Angeles Police Department (LAPD) says that patrol officers tried to talk with the man for about 75 minutes. They then declared an armed barricade and called the special weapons and tactics (SWAT) team. The LAPD sent in its Boston Dynamics Spot quadruped. The report states that a drone observed the sleeping man and the suspected gun before the quadruped entered. It adds that SWAT chose the quadruped because a tracked robot could not have climbed the bus steps. The report states that the quadruped climbed the bus steps and formed a barrier between the man and the suspected firearm. It does not describe the robot removing the weapon. The man woke, left the bus and was taken into custody about 6:40 a.m. The weapon was a BB gun (Police1). Police1 attributes the initial observation to the quadruped’s camera. International Business Times' October 2024 account says that the robot removed the gun. Deputy Chief David Kowalski approves each use. The robot cost nearly $300,000 (NBC). By 1 January 2025 SWAT had deployed the robot at least seven times, Spectrum News reported.

purpose: The department acquired the robot, in Deputy Chief Kowalski's words, “to save lives” by putting a camera and an articulating arm into dangerous scenes ahead of officers. This standoff was that use.

ratings.reason: A drone observed that the man was asleep. By the department's own report, the robot then stood between him and the gun. The two-hour standoff ended in an arrest with no injury reported. No source shows that officers would otherwise have been hurt.

The passengers had been evacuated before the robot was used, and the man was taken into custody unharmed. None of the reports ties either outcome to the robot. They describe the man waking and leaving the bus.
